articles.title: Nature doesn’t care about your climate conference speech
articles.summary: The article argues that Nepal faces a massive multi‑billion‑dollar adaptation shortfall as climate impacts worsen, while affluent countries continue to offer only rhetorical sympathy at international climate conferences. It criticizes the gap between lofty speeches and concrete financial support, highlighting how Nepal’s communities are already drowning in floods and landslides. The piece calls for urgent, tangible aid rather than empty promises, emphasizing the disparity between the needs of vulnerable nations and the limited assistance from wealthier states.

articles.title: Farmers face dire consequences as floods devastate Nepal’s harvest
articles.summary: Severe flooding across Nepal has ruined large swaths of the country's agricultural fields, threatening the upcoming harvest and jeopardizing food supplies. The disaster hits the very farmers who sustain the nation’s food security, leaving them with lost crops, damaged equipment, and uncertain incomes. Authorities warn that the loss could lead to higher food prices and increased hardship for rural households already vulnerable to climate shocks. Relief efforts are being mobilised, but the scale of damage underscores the urgent need for improved flood management and support for the farming community.

articles.title: ‘Bir Ganeshman’: A theatrical tribute to a freedom fighter
articles.summary: A new theatrical production honors Bir Ganeshman, a dedicated politician and freedom fighter, portraying his life and contributions at a time when Nepal is undergoing significant historical change. The play is described as a meaningful act of karma, reflecting the nation’s evolving identity and reverence for its past heroes.

articles.title: Flood damage leaves Rasuwagadhi road facing long repairs
articles.summary: Heavy rains caused the Bhotekoshi flood to wash away roughly 40 km of the Rasuwagadhi road, a crucial link to the Chinese border. The Department of Roads is responding by opening temporary tracks and planning the construction of Bailey bridges to restore connectivity. Officials aim to complete the repairs before the upcoming Dashain festival, emphasizing the road’s importance for trade and travel. The extensive damage suggests a prolonged reconstruction period, highlighting challenges in Nepal’s infrastructure resilience.

articles.title: Trapped nine days in a dark tunnel, Nepali man tells his survival story
articles.summary: Sanjay Sah, a Nepali man, survived being trapped for nine days in a dark tunnel after a collapse. He endured extreme darkness, hunger, injuries and isolation, relying on prayer, hope and thoughts of his family to stay alive. Rescue teams finally located and freed him after ten days underground. Sah recounted his ordeal, emphasizing the mental strength that helped him survive the harsh conditions.

articles.title: Two killed, four seriously injured in Rukum West jeep crash
articles.summary: A jeep traveling from Kotgaun to Khalanga in Rukum West district crashed into the Deuta Khola river within Sanibheri Rural Municipality-6. The accident resulted in two fatalities and four people sustaining serious injuries. Local authorities have been alerted to the incident, and emergency services are responding to the scene.

articles.title: India sends three Bailey bridges to restore flood-hit connectivity
articles.summary: India has dispatched three Bailey bridge components to Nepal to restore road connectivity after severe flooding in Nuwakot. The first shipment, containing parts for a 70‑metre bridge, arrived in Hetauda and will be assembled to re‑establish vital transport links disrupted by the disaster. The aid underscores ongoing cooperation between the two neighboring countries in disaster response and infrastructure recovery.

articles.title: Rescuers searching for 140 people from Indonesia passenger ship, official says
articles.summary: Rescuers are conducting a large-scale search for about 140 passengers missing from an Indonesian passenger ship after it encountered rough seas. Authorities report that the adverse weather conditions are hampering rescue efforts, and many passengers remain unaccounted for. The situation is being closely monitored as teams continue to locate survivors and recover bodies.

articles.title: The search dog helping find bodies buried by Nepal’s floods
articles.summary: A Labrador named Samba, trained to detect human remains, has assisted rescue teams in Rasuwa, Nepal, locating approximately 20 bodies buried under mud and debris after recent floods. The canine's work highlights the ongoing challenges of flood recovery and the role of specialized search dogs in disaster response.

articles.title: 18-km cross-border transmission line under MCC completed
articles.summary: The Nepalese segment of a 18‑km, 400 kV cross‑border transmission line connecting the New Butwal Substation to the Nepal‑India border has been completed. The line is now awaiting regulatory approvals and final procedures before it can be energized, marking a key step in enhancing bilateral power trade and grid stability between the two countries.

articles.title: Why can’t consumers exchange other brands’ LPG cylinders amid the shortage
articles.summary: The Nepalese government issued a directive permitting consumers to exchange LPG cylinders of different brands to alleviate a nationwide shortage. However, major gas distributors have reported that the policy cannot be implemented due to legal ambiguities, technical incompatibilities between cylinder types, and insurance liabilities. The stalemate leaves households without a viable solution, intensifying public frustration and highlighting gaps in regulatory coordination.

articles.title: At least 129 missing after Indonesian passenger ship capsizes
articles.summary: A passenger vessel named Virgo Transport 8 capsized off Indonesia, leaving at least 129 people missing. Rescue teams have so far saved 108 individuals and continue to search for additional survivors. The incident has prompted a large-scale rescue operation by local authorities and agencies.

articles.title: Vehicles cross Krishnabhir on Sunday in trial run after 11 days
articles.summary: After an 11‑day closure, about 20 vehicles—including a stranded gas tanker and several heavy trucks—were permitted to cross the temporary track at Krishnabhir on Sunday as part of a trial run. Authorities said the test shows the route is usable, but full regular traffic is expected to resume only after several more days of work.

articles.title: Nepalis cut back on food as ‘hyperinflation’ and shortages bite
articles.summary: Consumers in Kathmandu Valley are reducing food purchases and scaling back festive preparations as supply disruptions, soaring transport costs, and hyperinflation drive up the prices of daily essentials.

articles.title: Lawmakers want a shorter governor term. Experts fear instability in central bank
articles.summary: Lawmakers in Nepal are proposing to shorten the term of the Nepal Rastra Bank governor. Former governors and monetary experts warn that such a change could erode the central bank’s independence, lead to frequent leadership turnover, and disrupt policy continuity, potentially destabilising the country’s monetary policy and economic stability.

articles.title: What should Balendra Shah tell the world in New York?
articles.summary: Ahead of Nepal's prime minister's inaugural UN General Assembly speech, the article gathers perspectives from experts, leaders and activists on how the country should present its climate crisis on the global stage. It highlights the urgency of Nepal's environmental challenges, the need for international support, and suggestions for framing the narrative to attract attention and aid. Balendra Shah, Kathmandu's mayor, is asked what message he would convey in New York, emphasizing the country's vulnerability and potential contributions to climate solutions.

articles.title: Why Nepal’s climate crisis is also a public-health emergency
articles.summary: Nepal's climate crisis is also a public-health emergency, as seen in the Bhotekoshi flood.

articles.title: Nepal fell in love with EVs. It forgot to regulate them
articles.summary: Nepal's enthusiasm for electric vehicles has outpaced its regulatory framework. While imports of EVs and charging stations are rising, the country lacks a systematic certification process for the vehicles and especially their lithium‑ion batteries, exposing consumers to safety risks and undermining market confidence. Officials acknowledge the gap and call for a legal framework to test, approve, and monitor EVs, citing models from other nations where batteries are certified before sale.

articles.title: Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal on rebuilding after the Bhotekoshi floods
articles.summary: Infrastructure Development Minister Sunil Lamsal outlined the government's plan to rebuild communities affected by the Bhotekoshi floods. The strategy includes resettling displaced families, repairing and upgrading damaged roads and bridges, improving the China‑border crossing, and constructing safer settlements for disaster‑prone areas.

articles.title: Beijing signals support for rebuilding flood-ravaged Rasuwagadhi route
articles.summary: Nepal has requested Chinese assistance to rebuild the 16‑km Syaphrubesi‑Rasuwagadhi road damaged by floods, while the government prepares a temporary track to maintain access to the border crossing. Beijing has signaled support for the reconstruction, underscoring ongoing cooperation between the neighboring countries.

articles.title: A year later, the Gen Z movement lives on in art
articles.summary: A year after the Gen Z protests reshaped Nepal’s politics, artists across the country are using songs, theatre, photography and visual art to record, mourn and interpret the movement. The piece highlights how creative expression has become a means for young Nepalis to process the upheaval, preserve its memory and critique ongoing political developments. Through murals in Kathmandu, protest songs, stage performances and photo essays, the article shows how the spirit of the movement lives on in cultural spaces, influencing public discourse and offering a hopeful lens on future change.

articles.title: Booker-winning translator Deepa Bhasthi on why she has ‘nothing kind to say about AI’
articles.summary: Booker-winning translator Deepa Bhasthi discusses the importance of preserving the soul, musicality, and rhythm of a language in translation, criticizing AI's role in erasing cultural roots.

articles.title: Sweden’s centre-left bloc leads close election against right-wing government
articles.summary: Sweden's centre-left coalition, led by former prime minister Magdalena Andersson, has taken a narrow early lead in the upcoming election, challenging the incumbent right‑wing government of Ulf Kristersson. If the centre-left wins, it could end Kristersson's four‑year rule and prompt a reassessment of Sweden's increasingly strict migration policies. The race remains tight as votes are still being counted.

articles.title: Nepal tunnel survivor finds solace in village homecoming
articles.summary: After being rescued following nine days trapped in a hydropower tunnel collapse, Sanjay Sah returned to his village, where his family welcomed him. While his homecoming brings a moment of relief, the community continues to mourn the workers still missing from the disaster that occurred last month. The incident highlights ongoing safety concerns in Nepal's expanding hydropower sector and the emotional toll on affected families.

articles.title: Flood blocks Jajarkot-Dolpa road, sweeps away homes and shops
articles.summary: Heavy torrential rain caused severe flooding in the Nalgad area of Jajarkot district, Nepal, blocking the Jajarkot‑Dolpa road along the Bheri Corridor. The flood swept away homes, shops and other structures, disrupting transport and leaving residents displaced.
